title: Number of Russians with residence permits rose 61% in Spain after 2021, while falling in Latvia, Estonia, and Czechia
text: The number of Russian citizens holding valid residence permits in EU countries rose by nearly 105,000, or 14%, from 772,000 at the end of 2021 to 877,000 at the end of 2025. The Volna project reported the figures, citing Eurostat data . At the end of 2025, Germany had the most Russian citizens with temporary or permanent residency (218,000), followed by Spain (117,000), Estonia (78,000), France (67,000), and Serbia (63,000). Spain recorded the largest increase: the number of Russians holding residence permits there rose by 44,000, or 61%, over four years. Cyprus ranked second (up 27,000), followed by France (up 14,000). In some EU countries, however, the number of Russian citizens with temporary or permanent residency fell. The largest declines were in Latvia (down 15,000), Estonia (down 9,000), and Czechia (down 8,000). Eurostat data indicate that the number of Russians who had settled in the EU rose sharply in 2022 and 2023, then remained largely stable. text: Businessman Oleg Varyukhin, who traveled to Russia after living in Ukraine for 27 years, has been charged with treason for paying Ukraine’s mandatory military levy into its state budget, Mediazona reported. Varyukhin was detained in May 2026. In early August, his lawyer, Yuri Shel, said the treason charge stemmed from tax payments in Ukraine. At the time, it was unclear which tax the Russian authorities had taken issue with. Officers from Russia’s Federal Security Service found records of the tax payments on Varyukhin’s phone during a search at the airport, his lawyer said. Money transfers to support the Ukrainian army have previously led to treason prosecutions in Russia. But Varyukhin is the first person known to be prosecuted for treason for paying taxes into Ukraine’s state budget, Mediazona noted. Varyukhin was born in Norilsk and moved to Ukraine in 1999, where he ran a perfume shop. He was unable to obtain Ukrainian citizenship and did not have a Russian passport either : he had left Russia with Soviet documents. In 2026, he flew to Russia via Moldova to update his documents. title: Russia says it’s fighting scammers. Its latest proposals would push VPN services off Russian servers, tie eSIMs to devices, and expand telecom data retention.
text: Russia says it’s fighting scammers. Its latest proposals would push VPN services off Russian servers, tie eSIMs to devices, and expand telecom data retention. Fighting fraud has been a major focus of Russian lawmaking in recent years. The country has already adopted two sweeping packages of anti-fraud measures, and the authorities often use the fight against fraud as a pretext to push through repressive measures. This was their justification, for example, for banning voice and video calls on Telegram and WhatsApp. This week, Russia’s Digital Development Ministry published provisions from a third package aimed at telephone and online fraud. It includes another set of major proposals that could impose much tighter restrictions on internet use in Russia. Meduza reviewed the document and breaks down its key proposals. VPN services would find it harder to use Russian hosting providers Roskomnadzor, Russia’s communications regulator, would create a separate registry of Russian hosting providers’ customers who use rented computing resources to run proxy or VPN services that help circumvent internet censorship. text: Во Франции вновь украли произведение искусства — на этот раз уникальную книгу «Апокалипсис» весом 210 кг Кражи произведений искусства во Франции продолжаются. В ночь с 4 на 5 октября из Центра современного искусства в Иссуаре похитили «Апокалипсис святого Иоанна» — уникальную книгу весом около 210 кг. Примерно 150 кг приходится на ее бронзовый переплет, созданный Сальвадором Дали. Книгу создали в 1958–1961 годах по инициативе французского издателя Жозефа Форе. Над ней работали художники и писатели, среди которых Жан Кокто, Бернар Бюффе, Леонар Фужита и Эмиль Чоран. Экземпляр существует в единственном числе. Расследованием занимается жандармерия Клермон-Феррана. «Этой ночью убили Францию, убили французское культурное наследие», — заявил владелец произведения Кристиан Карутзос. 🎉 Подписывайся на Readovka в МАКС

text: Moscow Court Jails Ex-Sochi Mayor for 15 Years in Prison in Corruption Case Oct. 5, 2026 Alexei Kopaygorodsky and his wife in court. Dmitry Belitsky / Moskva News Agency A Moscow judge has sentenced the former mayor of the Black Sea resort city of Sochi to 15 years in maximum-security prison for corruption, state media reported Monday, citing the Russian Prosecutor General’s Office. Alexei Kopaygorodsky, 41, served as mayor from September 2019 until May 2024, when he abruptly resigned, citing a transition to a federal post. After the transfer failed to materialize, Kopaygorodsky joined a volunteer army battalion fighting in Ukraine. He was arrested in the Russian-occupied Luhansk region of eastern Ukraine in September 2024 and transferred to Moscow, where prosecutors sought 21 years in prison for him and 16 years for his wife. The Meshchansky District Court found Kopaygorodsky guilty of receiving large-scale bribes, embezzling municipal property and laundering criminal proceeds, according to Interfax. text: Russia Sentences ‘Masyanya’ Creator to 4 Years in Absentia Over Anti-War Cartoon Oct. 5, 2026 Oleg Kuvaev. Oleg Kuvaev (CC BY-SA 4.0) A St. Petersburg court has sentenced Oleg Kuvaev, creator of the animated series “Masyanya,” to four years and one month in prison in absentia over an episode that investigators said urged Russian soldiers to surrender or desert. The city’s Nevsky District Court found Kuvaev guilty of publicly calling for actions against state security and failing to comply with obligations imposed on people designated as “foreign agents,” the city courts’ press service said . The court also barred him from publishing online or administering websites for four years. Kuvaev has lived in Israel since 2006. Investigators said Kuvaev’s 2023 episode “Idoliada,” the 169th installment of “Masyanya,” contained calls for Russian servicemen to surrender, desert and disobey their commanders. The episode also promoted “I Want to Live,” a Ukrainian project that helps Russian soldiers surrender, according to investigators. title: Soviet TV Hypnotist Anatoly Kashpirovsky Dies at 87
text: Soviet TV Hypnotist Anatoly Kashpirovsky Dies at 87 Oct. 5, 2026 Anatoly Kashpirovsky. Anatoly Kashpirovsky / YouTube Anatoly Kashpirovsky, the Soviet-era hypnotist whose televised “healing sessions” drew enormous audiences in the late 1980s, died on Saturday in Moscow at the age of 87. “Anatoly Mikhailovich passed away from advanced cancer that had spread to his lungs and brain,” Kashpirovsky’s nephew Yury Mamayev told state media. “There was multiple organ failure, meaning that the affected organs simply stopped functioning as a result of the cancer,” the TASS news agency quoted Mamayev as saying. A representative said earlier that Kashpirovsky suffered “sudden” cardiac arrest following a sharp drop in blood pressure. Born in Soviet Ukraine in 1939, Kashpirovsky graduated from the Vinnitsa Medical Institute in 1962 and spent 25 years working as a psychiatrist in a regional psychiatric hospital. He became a household name in the 1980s as public interest in the occult grew across the country during Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev’s perestroika reforms. text: Ovechkin to Launch His Own Beer Brand in Russia Oct. 5, 2026 pivovarnibochkarev.ru Washington Capitals star Alexander Ovechkin plans to launch his own beer brand in Russia with a producer owned by Arnest, a group that has rapidly expanded by buying the Russian businesses of departing Western companies. The OVI range will be produced by Bochkarev Breweries and is expected to go on sale before the end of 2026, the Kommersant newspaper reported Monday. It will include a classic lager, a lower-alcohol lager and an alcohol-free beer, priced at about 100 rubles ($1.18) per can. The venture brings together one of Russia’s best-known athletes, whose support for President Vladimir Putin has drawn renewed criticism abroad, and a company that has become a major beneficiary of the Western corporate exodus since Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. “I have long wanted to create my own beer, one that I would enjoy drinking myself,” Ovechkin said in comments supplied to Kommersant by the brewer’s press office. text: Krasnodar Mayor Resigns After Contentious Tenure Oct. 5, 2026 Yevgeny Naumov. admkrai.krasnodar.ru Yevgeny Naumov, the mayor of the southern Russian city of Krasnodar, announced his early resignation on Monday. Naumov, whose five-year term was set to expire in November 2027, did not explain the reason behind his departure. The Krasnodar City Duma accepted Naumov’s resignation and appointed First Deputy Mayor Dmitry Vasilyev as acting head of the city. The City Duma will select the city's next mayor from a shortlist presented by Governor Veniamin Kondratyev. Kondratyev initiated a new selection process for mayoral candidates last month. Born in Krasnodar in 1980, Naumov spent his career within the municipal and regional administration. Local lawmakers elected him mayor in November 2022. Naumov’s four-year tenure was marked by local protests and controversies over infrastructure and urban planning decisions. Unfortunately, the Norman army had been held up in traffic on the A27 from Brighton, meaning the most significant battle in English history had to be delayed by 20 minutes while the French got into their costumes. On 14 October 1966, when a group of 500 students from Kent and Sussex universities met to re-enact the Battle of Hastings to mark its 900th anniversary, not every aspect was strictly historically accurate. Yes, the event was being staged on the same fields outside Battle in East Sussex where the original clash happened, but the English were wearing belted sacks and their swords and axes were made of wood and hardboard
author: Esther Addley

text: «Говорили, будет доллар по 45 при Зеленском, будет хаос в стране, будет война. Как-то, смотрите, ничего не случилось», — бахвалился Зеленский в 2020 году К сегодняшнему дню сбылось ровно всё, что украинская сторона когда-то называла «российской пропагандой». Курс доллара в обменниках превысил 45 гривен (до Майдана он колебался в пределах 5–8). Выборов нет и не предвидится т.к. "конституция на паузе", а война разгорелась в полную силу, и её западные кукловоды не собираются прекращать. Люди раньше не могли даже вообразить, что их будут, словно крыс, отлавливать на родных улицах и травить за всё подряд: за "ухилянство", за русский язык, за веру, за критику власти, за коррупцию в стране. Теперь, словно в насмешку, команда Зеленского развешивает по городам Незалежной плакаты с "диктатором-наркоманом" и призывом "улыбаться", пишет канал "На самом деле в Харькове". @ukr_2025_ru

text: Claude сдал юзера полиции — бот написал донос на жительницу Флориды после того, как заподозрил угрозу . Девушка использовала Claude как «дневник», но однажды написала, что хочет купить оружие и расстрелять офис шерифа . Бот отметил её как угрозу и передал информацию Anthropic, а компания сообщила в полицию. Девушку обвинили в письменной угрозе насилием — во Флориде это преступление второй степени. Переписку с Claude приобщили к делу как доказательство. Ууу, сука, цифровой гулаг
author: Boris Rozhin

text: Представлен российский беспилотный танк для городских боёв Тяжёлый штурмовой роботизированный комплекс (ТШРК) «Штурм» был продемонстрирован на стратегических командно-штабных учениях «Центр-2026» в Челябинской области. Машина представляет собой не просто танк без экипажа, а целое семейство специализированных боевых роботов, объединённых общей системой управления. Один расчёт может удалённо управлять сразу несколькими боевыми машинами в контуре единой системы поля боя, в которую входят также БПМТ «Спиридон» и наземные роботы «Импульс-М». Сам танк представляет собой модификацию Т-72/90 с укороченным 125-мм орудием. Он управляется дистанционно из машины поддержки, которая также размещена на базе танка Т-72. Дальность работы не заявлена, предположительно, она будет достаточно большой при задействовании спутниковой группировки «Рассвет». В дальнейшем к системе выбора целей также подключат искусственный интеллект. Укороченное орудие позволяет башне вращаться на 360° на узких улицах, не задевая стены, столбы и завалы. На крыше танка расположен блок из множества камер, дающих панорамный обзор. Автомат заряжания помещён в специальную капсулу, что повышает защищённость боекомплекта. Разработ

title: Moscow comes under large-scale drone attack – photos, videos
text: Moscow comes under large-scale drone attack – photos, videos Olha Hlushchenko — 6 October, 02:36 Column of smoke. Photo: Exilenova+ Посилання скопійовано Add UP as preferred source in Google The city of Moscow and Moscow Oblast have been attacked by 650 drones overnight, from the evening of 5 October until the morning of 6 October. title: Russian attacks on Kharkiv Oblast kill one and injure 20 people – photos
text: Russian attacks on Kharkiv Oblast kill one and injure 20 people – photos Olha Hlushchenko — 6 October, 00:20 Damage caused by a Russian attack. Source: Kharkiv Oblast Prosecutor's Office Details: At around 17:20 on 5 October, Russian forces attacked a car with an FPV drone on the Zolochiv-Derhachi road near the village of Maslii. title: Zelensky condemns 'horrific' Russian strike on boat carrying corn in Black Sea
text: Zelensky condemns 'horrific' Russian strike on boat carrying corn in Black Sea Image source, Romanian Interior Ministry via REUTERS Image caption, The fire-damaged vessel was pictured after Romanian authorities launched a rescue mission By Paulin Kola Published 5 October 2026 Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky has condemned a "horrific" Russian attack on a vessel carrying corn in the Black Sea. The ship's captain was killed in the strike involving two drones, Zelensky said, and another sailor was unaccounted for. Eleven crew members - nationals of Azerbaijan and India - have been rescued. Romania said it had mounted a rescue mission after "a fire on the ship Royad Mammadov" outside the country's territorial waters. It said two people had died. Russia has not commented, but its defence ministry earlier said it had struck two cargo vessels. Russia has been pounding Ukrainian infrastructure in what it says is retaliation for Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries and ships in the Black Sea. title: Moscow Court Jails Ex-Sochi Mayor for 15 Years in Prison in Corruption Case
text: Moscow Court Jails Ex-Sochi Mayor for 15 Years in Prison in Corruption Case Oct. 5, 2026 Alexei Kopaygorodsky and his wife in court. Dmitry Belitsky / Moskva News Agency A Moscow judge has sentenced the former mayor of the Black Sea resort city of Sochi to 15 years in maximum-security prison for corruption, state media reported Monday, citing the Russian Prosecutor General’s Office. Alexei Kopaygorodsky, 41, served as mayor from September 2019 until May 2024, when he abruptly resigned, citing a transition to a federal post. After the transfer failed to materialize, Kopaygorodsky joined a volunteer army battalion fighting in Ukraine. He was arrested in the Russian-occupied Luhansk region of eastern Ukraine in September 2024 and transferred to Moscow, where prosecutors sought 21 years in prison for him and 16 years for his wife. The Meshchansky District Court found Kopaygorodsky guilty of receiving large-scale bribes, embezzling municipal property and laundering criminal proceeds, according to Interfax. His wife Yanina Kopaygorodskaya was sentenced to 10 years in prison for serving as an accomplice, while her assistant Alexander Pasunko was fined 190,000 rubles ($2,200). Kopaygorodsk

text: Kremlin Downplays Estonia’s Troop Shift to Border, Plays Up Russia’s Intelligence Capabilities Oct. 5, 2026 Estonian military. mil.ee The Kremlin on Monday said Russia’s intelligence services were capable of monitoring military movements along the country’s borders, brushing aside reports that Estonia is shifting troops closer to the Russian border. “There should be no doubt that our Defense Ministry and other relevant services possess the necessary intelligence to properly monitor and assess the situation around our borders,” spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters during a daily briefing. His comments come in response to the Financial Times detailing Estonia’s strategic pivot toward an “active defense” posture after observing Russia’s military tactics in Ukraine. Under the updated doctrine, the Baltic nation of 1.3 million is moving primary combat units from northern Estonia’s Tapa to Jõhvi — 50 kilometers (31 miles) from the border with the Leningrad region. title: Russia Sentences ‘Masyanya’ Creator to 4 Years in Absentia Over Anti-War Cartoon
text: Russia Sentences ‘Masyanya’ Creator to 4 Years in Absentia Over Anti-War Cartoon Oct. 5, 2026 Oleg Kuvaev. Oleg Kuvaev (CC BY-SA 4.0) A St. Petersburg court has sentenced Oleg Kuvaev, creator of the animated series “Masyanya,” to four years and one month in prison in absentia over an episode that investigators said urged Russian soldiers to surrender or desert. The city’s Nevsky District Court found Kuvaev guilty of publicly calling for actions against state security and failing to comply with obligations imposed on people designated as “foreign agents,” the city courts’ press service said . The court also barred him from publishing online or administering websites for four years. Kuvaev has lived in Israel since 2006. Investigators said Kuvaev’s 2023 episode “Idoliada,” the 169th installment of “Masyanya,” contained calls for Russian servicemen to surrender, desert and disobey their commanders. The episode also promoted “I Want to Live,” a Ukrainian project that helps Russian soldiers surrender, according to investigators. title: Soviet TV Hypnotist Anatoly Kashpirovsky Dies at 87
text: Soviet TV Hypnotist Anatoly Kashpirovsky Dies at 87 Oct. 5, 2026 Anatoly Kashpirovsky. Anatoly Kashpirovsky / YouTube Anatoly Kashpirovsky, the Soviet-era hypnotist whose televised “healing sessions” drew enormous audiences in the late 1980s, died on Saturday in Moscow at the age of 87. “Anatoly Mikhailovich passed away from advanced cancer that had spread to his lungs and brain,” Kashpirovsky’s nephew Yury Mamayev told state media. “There was multiple organ failure, meaning that the affected organs simply stopped functioning as a result of the cancer,” the TASS news agency quoted Mamayev as saying. A representative said earlier that Kashpirovsky suffered “sudden” cardiac arrest following a sharp drop in blood pressure. Born in Soviet Ukraine in 1939, Kashpirovsky graduated from the Vinnitsa Medical Institute in 1962 and spent 25 years working as a psychiatrist in a regional psychiatric hospital. He became a household name in the 1980s as public interest in the occult grew across the country during Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev’s perestroika reforms. title: Ovechkin to Launch His Own Beer Brand in Russia
text: Ovechkin to Launch His Own Beer Brand in Russia Oct. 5, 2026 pivovarnibochkarev.ru Washington Capitals star Alexander Ovechkin plans to launch his own beer brand in Russia with a producer owned by Arnest, a group that has rapidly expanded by buying the Russian businesses of departing Western companies. The OVI range will be produced by Bochkarev Breweries and is expected to go on sale before the end of 2026, the Kommersant newspaper reported Monday. It will include a classic lager, a lower-alcohol lager and an alcohol-free beer, priced at about 100 rubles ($1.18) per can. The venture brings together one of Russia’s best-known athletes, whose support for President Vladimir Putin has drawn renewed criticism abroad, and a company that has become a major beneficiary of the Western corporate exodus since Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. “I have long wanted to create my own beer, one that I would enjoy drinking myself,” Ovechkin said in comments supplied to Kommersant by the brewer’s press office. title: Krasnodar Mayor Resigns After Contentious Tenure
text: Krasnodar Mayor Resigns After Contentious Tenure Oct. 5, 2026 Yevgeny Naumov. admkrai.krasnodar.ru Yevgeny Naumov, the mayor of the southern Russian city of Krasnodar, announced his early resignation on Monday. Naumov, whose five-year term was set to expire in November 2027, did not explain the reason behind his departure. The Krasnodar City Duma accepted Naumov’s resignation and appointed First Deputy Mayor Dmitry Vasilyev as acting head of the city. The City Duma will select the city's next mayor from a shortlist presented by Governor Veniamin Kondratyev. Kondratyev initiated a new selection process for mayoral candidates last month. Born in Krasnodar in 1980, Naumov spent his career within the municipal and regional administration. Local lawmakers elected him mayor in November 2022. Naumov’s four-year tenure was marked by local protests and controversies over infrastructure and urban planning decisions. In January, he signed off on plans to build an Orthodox Church on the grounds of a riverside park despite opposition from residents. Since November 2025, more than 30,000 people have signed a petition demanding his resignation. A local court began hearing a lawsuit against Naumov

The female employee of the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East was hospitalized last Tuesday with symptoms of severe pneumonia and died on Thursday. title: Dozens Detained at Moscow Communist Party Rally
text: Dozens Detained at Moscow Communist Party Rally Oct. 5, 2026 SOTAvision Moscow police detained around 60 people on Sunday during a Communist Party rally commemorating the 1993 constitutional crisis, after the event spiraled into a protest against alleged fraud during last month’s parliamentary elections. An estimated 2,000 people gathered for an annual memorial honoring those killed during an Oct. 4, 1993, standoff when President Boris Yeltsin ordered tanks to shell the Supreme Soviet parliament building to dissolve opposition to his administration. Eyewitnesses told the Telegram news channel Ostorozhno Novosti that police officers charged into the crowd after chants of slogans like “Down with the Tsar!” “Freedom for political prisoners!” and “For fair elections!” broke out against the ruling United Russia party. United Russia won a record number of seats in the State Duma during the country’s first wartime parliamentary elections last month. The Communist Party — the largest Kremlin-approved systemic opposition faction — won fewer seats than in previous elections. title: Skull fractures suggest servants of Egypt’s ancient kings were sacrificed
text: A fresco depicting a funeral procession in ancient Egypt. Photograph: DEA/F Guenet/De Agostini/Getty Images View image in fullscreen A fresco depicting a funeral procession in ancient Egypt. If the the bacteria reach the lungs, they cause pneumonic plague. Pneumonic plague is highly contagious as it can pass from person to person through the air, via coughing, for example. title: Rubio visits Iceland ‘to discuss security collaboration’ as US boosts Arctic presence
text: Advertising Rubio visits Iceland ‘to discuss security collaboration’ as US boosts Arctic presence Europe US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is set to travel to Iceland on Monday, two weeks after Washington sealed a security pact with Denmark and Greenland on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly. title: Suspected pneumonic plague in Siberia: What we know about the disease
text: Health Russian Federation Suspected pneumonic plague in Siberia: What to know Kaukab Shairani | Nicolas Martin 10/05/2026 October 5, 2026 A worker at a plague research institute in Siberia has died, and nearly 200 of her contacts are under medical observation. Russian authorities deny a link to the bacterial infection. The US is monitoring the situation. https://p.dw.com/p/5Nm2x Image: Britta Pedersen/dpa/picture alliance Advertisement What you need to know about plague There are three forms of plague, all caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis. The three forms of plague are bubonic, septicemic and pneumonic. Bubonic plague is the most common form, it does not spread from person to person. If untreated, the bacteria can move through the body and bloodstream, causing septicemic plague, which causes internal bleeding and organ failure. If the the bacteria reach the lungs, they cause pneumonic plague. Pneumonic plague is highly contagious as it can pass from person to person through the air, via coughing, for example. text: Moscow Court Jails Ex-Sochi Mayor for 15 Years in Prison in Corruption Case Oct. 5, 2026 Alexei Kopaygorodsky and his wife in court. Alexei Kopaygorodsky, 41, served as mayor from September 2019 until May 2024, when he abruptly resigned, citing a transition to a federal post. He was arrested in the Russian-occupied Luhansk region of eastern Ukraine in September 2024 and transferred to Moscow, where prosecutors sought 21 years in prison for him and 16 years for his wife. The Meshchansky District Court found Kopaygorodsky guilty of receiving large-scale bribes, embezzling municipal property and laundering criminal proceeds, according to Interfax. text: Russia Sentences ‘Masyanya’ Creator to 4 Years in Absentia Over Anti-War Cartoon Oct. 5, 2026 Oleg Kuvaev. Oleg Kuvaev (CC BY-SA 4.0) A St. Petersburg court has sentenced Oleg Kuvaev, creator of the animated series “Masyanya,” to four years and one month in prison in absentia over an episode that investigators said urged Russian soldiers to surrender or desert. The city’s Nevsky District Court found Kuvaev guilty of publicly calling for actions against state security and failing to comply with obligations imposed on people designated as “foreign agents,” the city courts’ press service said . The court also barred him from publishing online or administering websites for four years. Kuvaev has lived in Israel since 2006. Investigators said Kuvaev’s 2023 episode “Idoliada,” the 169th installment of “Masyanya,” contained calls for Russian servicemen to surrender, desert and disobey their commanders. The episode also promoted “I Want to Live,” a Ukrainian project that helps Russian soldiers surrender, according to investigators. title: Soviet TV Hypnotist Anatoly Kashpirovsky Dies at 87
text: Soviet TV Hypnotist Anatoly Kashpirovsky Dies at 87 Oct. 5, 2026 Anatoly Kashpirovsky. Anatoly Kashpirovsky / YouTube Anatoly Kashpirovsky, the Soviet-era hypnotist whose televised “healing sessions” drew enormous audiences in the late 1980s, died on Saturday in Moscow at the age of 87. “Anatoly Mikhailovich passed away from advanced cancer that had spread to his lungs and brain,” Kashpirovsky’s nephew Yury Mamayev told state media. “There was multiple organ failure, meaning that the affected organs simply stopped functioning as a result of the cancer,” the TASS news agency quoted Mamayev as saying. A representative said earlier that Kashpirovsky suffered “sudden” cardiac arrest following a sharp drop in blood pressure. Born in Soviet Ukraine in 1939, Kashpirovsky graduated from the Vinnitsa Medical Institute in 1962 and spent 25 years working as a psychiatrist in a regional psychiatric hospital. He became a household name in the 1980s as public interest in the occult grew across the country during Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev’s perestroika reforms. title: Ovechkin to Launch His Own Beer Brand in Russia
text: Ovechkin to Launch His Own Beer Brand in Russia Oct. 5, 2026 pivovarnibochkarev.ru Washington Capitals star Alexander Ovechkin plans to launch his own beer brand in Russia with a producer owned by Arnest, a group that has rapidly expanded by buying the Russian businesses of departing Western companies. The OVI range will be produced by Bochkarev Breweries and is expected to go on sale before the end of 2026, the Kommersant newspaper reported Monday. It will include a classic lager, a lower-alcohol lager and an alcohol-free beer, priced at about 100 rubles ($1.18) per can. The venture brings together one of Russia’s best-known athletes, whose support for President Vladimir Putin has drawn renewed criticism abroad, and a company that has become a major beneficiary of the Western corporate exodus since Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. “I have long wanted to create my own beer, one that I would enjoy drinking myself,” Ovechkin said in comments supplied to Kommersant by the brewer’s press office. title: Krasnodar Mayor Resigns After Contentious Tenure
text: Krasnodar Mayor Resigns After Contentious Tenure Oct. 5, 2026 Yevgeny Naumov. admkrai.krasnodar.ru Yevgeny Naumov, the mayor of the southern Russian city of Krasnodar, announced his early resignation on Monday. Naumov, whose five-year term was set to expire in November 2027, did not explain the reason behind his departure. The Krasnodar City Duma accepted Naumov’s resignation and appointed First Deputy Mayor Dmitry Vasilyev as acting head of the city. The City Duma will select the city's next mayor from a shortlist presented by Governor Veniamin Kondratyev. Kondratyev initiated a new selection process for mayoral candidates last month. Born in Krasnodar in 1980, Naumov spent his career within the municipal and regional administration. Local lawmakers elected him mayor in November 2022. Naumov’s four-year tenure was marked by local protests and controversies over infrastructure and urban planning decisions. In January, he signed off on plans to build an Orthodox Church on the grounds of a riverside park despite opposition from residents. Since November 2025, more than 30,000 people have signed a petition demanding his resignation. A local court began hearing a lawsuit against Naumov

title: Soviet TV Hypnotist Anatoly Kashpirovsky Dies at 87
text: Soviet TV Hypnotist Anatoly Kashpirovsky Dies at 87 Oct. 5, 2026 Anatoly Kashpirovsky. Anatoly Kashpirovsky / YouTube Anatoly Kashpirovsky, the Soviet-era hypnotist whose televised “healing sessions” drew enormous audiences in the late 1980s, died on Saturday in Moscow at the age of 87. “Anatoly Mikhailovich passed away from advanced cancer that had spread to his lungs and brain,” Kashpirovsky’s nephew Yury Mamayev told state media. “There was multiple organ failure, meaning that the affected organs simply stopped functioning as a result of the cancer,” the TASS news agency quoted Mamayev as saying. A representative said earlier that Kashpirovsky suffered “sudden” cardiac arrest following a sharp drop in blood pressure. Born in Soviet Ukraine in 1939, Kashpirovsky graduated from the Vinnitsa Medical Institute in 1962 and spent 25 years working as a psychiatrist in a regional psychiatric hospital. He became a household name in the 1980s as public interest in the occult grew across the country during Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev’s perestroika reforms. Soviet Central Television started airing his six-part program, “Health Sessions of Psychotherapist Anatoly Kashpirovsky,” in Octobe

title: Ovechkin to Launch His Own Beer Brand in Russia
text: Ovechkin to Launch His Own Beer Brand in Russia Oct. 5, 2026 pivovarnibochkarev.ru Washington Capitals star Alexander Ovechkin plans to launch his own beer brand in Russia with a producer owned by Arnest, a group that has rapidly expanded by buying the Russian businesses of departing Western companies. The OVI range will be produced by Bochkarev Breweries and is expected to go on sale before the end of 2026, the Kommersant newspaper reported Monday. It will include a classic lager, a lower-alcohol lager and an alcohol-free beer, priced at about 100 rubles ($1.18) per can. The venture brings together one of Russia’s best-known athletes, whose support for President Vladimir Putin has drawn renewed criticism abroad, and a company that has become a major beneficiary of the Western corporate exodus since Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. “I have long wanted to create my own beer, one that I would enjoy drinking myself,” Ovechkin said in comments supplied to Kommersant by the brewer’s press office. He said he preferred pale beers with a clean, balanced taste. Bochkarev Breweries belongs to businessman Alexei Sagal’s Arnest group. Its brewing business was built around Heineken’s Ru

title: Krasnodar Mayor Resigns After Contentious Tenure
text: Krasnodar Mayor Resigns After Contentious Tenure Oct. 5, 2026 Yevgeny Naumov. admkrai.krasnodar.ru Yevgeny Naumov, the mayor of the southern Russian city of Krasnodar, announced his early resignation on Monday. Naumov, whose five-year term was set to expire in November 2027, did not explain the reason behind his departure. The Krasnodar City Duma accepted Naumov’s resignation and appointed First Deputy Mayor Dmitry Vasilyev as acting head of the city. The City Duma will select the city's next mayor from a shortlist presented by Governor Veniamin Kondratyev. Kondratyev initiated a new selection process for mayoral candidates last month. Born in Krasnodar in 1980, Naumov spent his career within the municipal and regional administration. Local lawmakers elected him mayor in November 2022. Naumov’s four-year tenure was marked by local protests and controversies over infrastructure and urban planning decisions. In January, he signed off on plans to build an Orthodox Church on the grounds of a riverside park despite opposition from residents. Since November 2025, more than 30,000 people have signed a petition demanding his resignation. A local court began hearing a lawsuit against Naumov

The men and boys now held in Iraq are living in 'dire' conditions, including deaths from illness, allegations of torture, and serious questions surrounding access to effective legal representation. title: Zelensky condemns 'horrific' Russian strike on boat carrying corn in Black Sea
text: Zelensky condemns 'horrific' Russian strike on boat carrying corn in Black Sea Image source, Romanian Interior Ministry via REUTERS Image caption, The fire-damaged vessel was pictured after Romanian authorities launched a rescue mission By Paulin Kola Published 5 October 2026 Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky has condemned a "horrific" Russian attack on a vessel carrying corn in the Black Sea. The ship's captain was killed in the strike involving two drones, Zelensky said, and another sailor was unaccounted for. Eleven crew members - nationals of Azerbaijan and India - have been rescued. Romania said it had mounted a rescue mission after "a fire on the ship Royad Mammadov" outside the country's territorial waters. It said two people had died. Russia has not commented, but its defence ministry earlier said it had struck two cargo vessels. Russia has been pounding Ukrainian infrastructure in what it says is retaliation for Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries and ships in the Black Sea. His comments come in response to the Financial Times detailing Estonia’s strategic pivot toward an “active defense” posture after observing Russia’s military tactics in Ukraine. Under the updated doctrine, the Baltic nation of 1.3 million is moving primary combat units from northern Estonia’s Tapa to Jõhvi — 50 kilometers (31 miles) from the border with the Leningrad region. title: Russia Sentences ‘Masyanya’ Creator to 4 Years in Absentia Over Anti-War Cartoon
text: Russia Sentences ‘Masyanya’ Creator to 4 Years in Absentia Over Anti-War Cartoon Oct. 5, 2026 Oleg Kuvaev. Oleg Kuvaev (CC BY-SA 4.0) A St. Petersburg court has sentenced Oleg Kuvaev, creator of the animated series “Masyanya,” to four years and one month in prison in absentia over an episode that investigators said urged Russian soldiers to surrender or desert. The city’s Nevsky District Court found Kuvaev guilty of publicly calling for actions against state security and failing to comply with obligations imposed on people designated as “foreign agents,” the city courts’ press service said . The court also barred him from publishing online or administering websites for four years. Kuvaev has lived in Israel since 2006. Investigators said Kuvaev’s 2023 episode “Idoliada,” the 169th installment of “Masyanya,” contained calls for Russian servicemen to surrender, desert and disobey their commanders. The episode also promoted “I Want to Live,” a Ukrainian project that helps Russian soldiers surrender, according to investigators. title: Soviet TV Hypnotist Anatoly Kashpirovsky Dies at 87
text: Soviet TV Hypnotist Anatoly Kashpirovsky Dies at 87 Oct. 5, 2026 Anatoly Kashpirovsky. Anatoly Kashpirovsky / YouTube Anatoly Kashpirovsky, the Soviet-era hypnotist whose televised “healing sessions” drew enormous audiences in the late 1980s, died on Saturday in Moscow at the age of 87. “Anatoly Mikhailovich passed away from advanced cancer that had spread to his lungs and brain,” Kashpirovsky’s nephew Yury Mamayev told state media. “There was multiple organ failure, meaning that the affected organs simply stopped functioning as a result of the cancer,” the TASS news agency quoted Mamayev as saying. A representative said earlier that Kashpirovsky suffered “sudden” cardiac arrest following a sharp drop in blood pressure. Born in Soviet Ukraine in 1939, Kashpirovsky graduated from the Vinnitsa Medical Institute in 1962 and spent 25 years working as a psychiatrist in a regional psychiatric hospital. He became a household name in the 1980s as public interest in the occult grew across the country during Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev’s perestroika reforms. Soviet Central Television started airing his six-part program, “Health Sessions of Psychotherapist Anatoly Kashpirovsky,” in Octobe

title: Ovechkin to Launch His Own Beer Brand in Russia
text: Ovechkin to Launch His Own Beer Brand in Russia Oct. 5, 2026 pivovarnibochkarev.ru Washington Capitals star Alexander Ovechkin plans to launch his own beer brand in Russia with a producer owned by Arnest, a group that has rapidly expanded by buying the Russian businesses of departing Western companies. The OVI range will be produced by Bochkarev Breweries and is expected to go on sale before the end of 2026, the Kommersant newspaper reported Monday. It will include a classic lager, a lower-alcohol lager and an alcohol-free beer, priced at about 100 rubles ($1.18) per can. The venture brings together one of Russia’s best-known athletes, whose support for President Vladimir Putin has drawn renewed criticism abroad, and a company that has become a major beneficiary of the Western corporate exodus since Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. “I have long wanted to create my own beer, one that I would enjoy drinking myself,” Ovechkin said in comments supplied to Kommersant by the brewer’s press office. He said he preferred pale beers with a clean, balanced taste. Bochkarev Breweries belongs to businessman Alexei Sagal’s Arnest group. Its brewing business was built around Heineken’s Ru

title: Krasnodar Mayor Resigns After Contentious Tenure
text: Krasnodar Mayor Resigns After Contentious Tenure Oct. 5, 2026 Yevgeny Naumov. admkrai.krasnodar.ru Yevgeny Naumov, the mayor of the southern Russian city of Krasnodar, announced his early resignation on Monday. Naumov, whose five-year term was set to expire in November 2027, did not explain the reason behind his departure. The Krasnodar City Duma accepted Naumov’s resignation and appointed First Deputy Mayor Dmitry Vasilyev as acting head of the city. The City Duma will select the city's next mayor from a shortlist presented by Governor Veniamin Kondratyev. Kondratyev initiated a new selection process for mayoral candidates last month. Born in Krasnodar in 1980, Naumov spent his career within the municipal and regional administration. Local lawmakers elected him mayor in November 2022. Naumov’s four-year tenure was marked by local protests and controversies over infrastructure and urban planning decisions. In January, he signed off on plans to build an Orthodox Church on the grounds of a riverside park despite opposition from residents. Since November 2025, more than 30,000 people have signed a petition demanding his resignation. A local court began hearing a lawsuit against Naumov

text: Officials Seek to Reassure Public After Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute Worker’s Death Oct. 5, 2026 The hospital in Shelekhov, Irkutsk region. yandex.ru/maps Russian health authorities maintain that the health situation in Siberia’s Irkutsk region remains stable amid concerns surrounding the death of a lab worker at a local anti-plague facility, state media reported Sunday. The female employee of the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East was hospitalized last Tuesday with symptoms of severe pneumonia and died on Thursday. The lab worker was diagnosed with “pneumonia of unknown etiology,” according to a statement from consumer safety watchdog Rospotrebnadzor cited by Interfax. Media reports have described the suspected infection as pneumonic plague, which affects the lungs and can spread between humans through respiratory droplets. Alexei Tsydenov, head of the neighboring republic of Buryatia, initially claimed the employee had died of the plague, before modifying his statement with the word “maybe.” Rospotrebnadzor said that laboratory analysis of material from the patient did not reveal any microorganisms associated with her work handling dangerous patho

title: Dozens Detained at Moscow Communist Party Rally
text: Dozens Detained at Moscow Communist Party Rally Oct. 5, 2026 SOTAvision Moscow police detained around 60 people on Sunday during a Communist Party rally commemorating the 1993 constitutional crisis, after the event spiraled into a protest against alleged fraud during last month’s parliamentary elections. An estimated 2,000 people gathered for an annual memorial honoring those killed during an Oct. 4, 1993, standoff when President Boris Yeltsin ordered tanks to shell the Supreme Soviet parliament building to dissolve opposition to his administration. United Russia won a record number of seats in the State Duma during the country’s first wartime parliamentary elections last month. title: Zelensky condemns 'horrific' Russian strike on boat carrying corn in Black Sea
text: Zelensky condemns 'horrific' Russian strike on boat carrying corn in Black Sea Image source, Romanian Interior Ministry via REUTERS Image caption, The fire-damaged vessel was pictured after Romanian authorities launched a rescue mission By Paulin Kola Published 5 October 2026 Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky has condemned a "horrific" Russian attack on a vessel carrying corn in the Black Sea. The ship's captain was killed in the strike involving two drones, Zelensky said, and another sailor was unaccounted for. Eleven crew members - nationals of Azerbaijan and India - have been rescued. Romania said it had mounted a rescue mission after "a fire on the ship Royad Mammadov" outside the country's territorial waters. It said two people had died. Russia has not commented, but its defence ministry earlier said it had struck two cargo vessels. Russia has been pounding Ukrainian infrastructure in what it says is retaliation for Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries and ships in the Black Sea. title: Moscow Court Jails Ex-Sochi Mayor for 15 Years in Prison in Corruption Case
text: Moscow Court Jails Ex-Sochi Mayor for 15 Years in Prison in Corruption Case Oct. 5, 2026 Alexei Kopaygorodsky and his wife in court. Dmitry Belitsky / Moskva News Agency A Moscow judge has sentenced the former mayor of the Black Sea resort city of Sochi to 15 years in maximum-security prison for corruption, state media reported Monday, citing the Russian Prosecutor General’s Office. Alexei Kopaygorodsky, 41, served as mayor from September 2019 until May 2024, when he abruptly resigned, citing a transition to a federal post. After the transfer failed to materialize, Kopaygorodsky joined a volunteer army battalion fighting in Ukraine. He was arrested in the Russian-occupied Luhansk region of eastern Ukraine in September 2024 and transferred to Moscow, where prosecutors sought 21 years in prison for him and 16 years for his wife. The Meshchansky District Court found Kopaygorodsky guilty of receiving large-scale bribes, embezzling municipal property and laundering criminal proceeds, according to Interfax. His wife Yanina Kopaygorodskaya was sentenced to 10 years in prison for serving as an accomplice, while her assistant Alexander Pasunko was fined 190,000 rubles ($2,200). Kopaygorodsk
